description: Source code for a browser automation module using chromiumoxide, managing browser state, events, and interactions.

classes.name: BrowserEvent
classes.description: Enumeration of browser events: state changes and errors.

classes.name: InnerState
classes.description: Represents the internal state of the browser automation, including current kind and shared data.

classes.name: InnerStateKind
classes.description: Enumeration of possible internal states: Pausing, Paused, Resuming, Navigating, Loading, Running, Acting.

classes.name: InnerEvent
classes.description: Enumeration of internal events triggering state transitions.

classes.name: StateRequestReason
classes.description: Reasons for requesting a new browser state.

classes.name: Timeout
classes.description: Type alias for Duration, representing timeouts.

classes.name: BrowserContext
classes.description: Context holding references to browser page, event channels, and control data.

classes.name: LaunchOptions
classes.description: Configuration options for launching the browser.

classes.name: Emulation
classes.description: Device emulation parameters like size and scale.

classes.name: BrowserOptions
classes.description: Options for browser instantiation including emulation, target creation, and instrumentation.

classes.name: DebuggerOptions
classes.description: Options for attaching to external or managed debugger instances.

classes.name: Browser
classes.description: Main class managing browser lifecycle, events, and actions.

methods.name: Browser::new
methods.description: Creates and initializes a new browser instance with specified options.

methods.name: Browser::initiate
methods.description: Starts the browser session, navigating to origin if configured.

methods.name: Browser::terminate
methods.description: Gracefully shuts down the browser session.

methods.name: Browser::apply
methods.description: Applies a browser action with a timeout.

methods.name: Browser::ensure_script_evaluated
methods.description: Ensures a script is evaluated in the page context.
